item.title: 🔴 OpenSSH auth bypass bug hits Alpine Linux, OperWRT
item.description:
Why this matters: Authentication bypass — review access controls and look for unauthorized access.
An OpenSSH authentication bypass bug hits Alpine Linux and OpenWRT, hackers attempt to raise fridge temperatures at French blood banks, a French bank gets hacked for $133 million, and the Thai opposition has been targeted with spyware.

Source: Risky Business News  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 8h

item.title: 🔴 DigiCert data breach exposes customer information, identity documents
item.description:
Why this matters: Potential data exposure — review monitoring and incident-response readiness.
DigiCert warns it suffered a data breach after a server migration mistakenly exposed an internal business system to the internet, allowing unauthorized access to customer information and identity documents. [...]

Source: BleepingComputer  |  Severity: Critical  |  Age: 19h

item.title: 🟠 Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality-system impact — consider guest services, PMS/POS, and property operations.

Tracked as CVE-2026-107441, the out-of-bounds write flaw could allow attackers to execute OS commands via crafted HTTP requests.

The post Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.



Source: SecurityWeek  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 1d

item.title: 🔴 Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
item.description:
Why this matters: Potentially urgent issue — confirm whether your environment is exposed.
Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found. The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without logging in. Zyxel has released new firmware for 10 GS1900 models that closes the hole. item.description:

item.title: 🟠 Zyxel fixes zero-day exploited to hack nearly 1,000 network switches
item.description:
Why this matters: Credential/phishing risk — reinforce MFA and watch for suspicious sign-ins.
Zyxel has patched a zero-day vulnerability in its GS1900 series network switches that hackers exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide and steal configuration files and credentials. [...]

item.description:
